candidate.mistake_reason: At Step 16, the agent asserted that the October 1949 SS Ile de France breakfast menu did not specify fruits beyond grapefruit juice and concluded that none of the painting’s fruits (watermelon, pears, lemons) were served. This misread or failed to properly extract the detailed GG Archives menu content, which typically lists specific fruits, and prematurely concluded "None" without verifying the actual fruit list.
candidate.first_mistake: This is the first step that directly produced the incorrect final outcome. Prior steps were evidence gathering; the erroneous "None" conclusion originates here based on an incomplete/incorrect interpretation of the menu.
candidate.mistake_not_corrected: No later agent corrected this conclusion. The orchestrator adopted the "None" result in Step 17 and finalized it, so the error propagated unchallenged.

This is plausibly the first error that directly yields the final wrong outcome and it wasn’t corrected later. The only weak part of the partner’s argument is the speculative claim that the GG Archives menu "typically lists specific fruits"—that detail isn’t verified in the log. Still, the core critique (premature conclusion without verifying the actual fruit list) is valid and grounded in the log.

Sound. This is an argument from ignorance and not grounded in extracted menu details (the page content was not shown). Earlier steps are exploratory (identifying the painting’s fruits and the ship) and do not themselves produce a wrong conclusion, nor is there evidence in the log that those earlier identifications are incorrect. No later step corrects the "None" conclusion. Thus, Step 16 is the first mistake leading to the incorrect outcome and remains uncorrected.
